editorial:
Imagine waking up in 2030 where the economy has totally crashed and the planet is overheating. You are stuck in a world where the only way to survive is to get a ticket to a safe zone, but the process is rigged. You follow a man who works for the Humanity Bureau, the group in charge of picking who gets to leave and who stays behind to suffer. The vibe is very tense and gritty, making you feel the desperation of people who have absolutely nothing left to lose. It feels like a race against time where trust is a luxury nobody can afford.

What really works here is how the tension builds as you realize the system is far more corrupt than it first seems. The acting is solid, though some parts of the plot move a bit slow in the middle. If you love stories about government secrets and survival, you should definitely give this a shot.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head when the truth about the selection process is revealed. You find out that the bureau isn't actually saving the best people, but is using the system to maintain power and control. The main characters fight back to expose the lies to the public. In the end, the corrupt leaders are brought down, giving the common people a real chance at a fair future and a way out of the ruins.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dystopian futures and government conspiracy stories.
